notes: Blockbench 5.2.2 web app (the same build as web.blockbench.net) built with `npm run build-web` (esbuild) and assembled into .ui-capture/out by .ui-capture/build_out.sh (index.html, dist/bundle.js, css, assets, font, lib, content). The front end needs no backend. Tooling: node 24.22.3 via mise.toml (matches CI). Data: Blockbench web keeps its user state in the browser, so .ui-capture/seed/seed_loader.js (a separate classic script injected before the bundle in out/index.html) seeds it on first load from out/seed/*.json, which .ui-capture/seed/generate.mjs produces: (1) localStorage settings of a long-time user (username 'mossbyte', ~148 launches, custom palette and color history, recently used actions); (2) the IndexedDB 'auto_backups' store that Blockbench uses for project recovery, holding 6 projects in the native .bbmodel 5.0 format (146 cubes, 14 animations total, each with editor_state: camera, selected element, saved flag) with generated pixel-art textures: red_panda (Bedrock entity, 15 cubes, 5 animations incl. a WIP climb), goblin_merchant (Bedrock entity with backpack/lantern/wares, 5 animations), sky_skiff_mk2 (Generic model airship, 76 cubes, 3 animations), copper_lantern_post (Java block, 4 textures, display transforms), mossy_mushroom_stool (Java block), ember_wisp (small Bedrock entity). After the app boots, the loader opens them with Blockbench's own AutoBackup.recoverAllBackups() (the 'Recover' action on the start screen) and focuses red_panda, so the editor opens with six project tabs. Open /?start to land on the start screen instead (it shows the 'Recover backup' banner plus model format list). Main areas: menu bar, project tabs, Edit/Paint/Animate modes (toolbar top right), 3D viewport, UV editor + Textures panel (left), Transform/Element and Outliner panels (right), Animate mode timeline/animations list, Display mode (Java block models), File > Plugins (store backed by the stub catalog), Settings, Keybindings. The browser needs WebGL. Rebuild everything with .ui-capture/build_out.sh; .ui-capture/tools/check.mjs is the headless screenshot check used during setup (serves out/ on :5471). The only console error is the app trying to register ./service_worker.js, which the web build does not produce without `npm run pwa`; it is harmless.
